title: The Book I Was Saving for Later
scene: You buy a book and keep waiting for the perfect time to read it. When you finally start, a review you saw on your phone changes how you read the book, until you realise you are evaluating the review rather than simply reading.
sceneJa: 買った本を『ちゃんと楽しめる完璧なタイミング』まで取っておく。ようやく読み始める直前にスマホで否定的なレビューを見てしまい、本そのものよりレビューが正しいかを確認する読み方になっていることに気づく。

questions.question: Which chunking is most natural?
options: I realised I was no longer reading the book / so much as checking / whether a stranger had reviewed it correctly
I realised / I was no longer / reading the book so much / as checking whether a stranger had reviewed it correctly
I realised I was / no longer reading / the book so / much as checking
questions.explanation: The first version keeps the realisation, the contrast phrase, and the clause explaining what the speaker was actually doing in clear meaning groups.

questions.question: What does ‘shouldn’t make much difference’ mean here?
options: The review should not have much influence on the speaker
The review should change the ending of the book
The reviewer should rewrite the review
questions.explanation: ‘Make much difference’ means have a significant effect. The speaker knows one review should not strongly affect the reading experience.

questions.question: What does the speaker realise after about twenty pages?
options: They are enjoying the book more than expected
They are paying more attention to testing the review than to reading the book itself
They have already read the book before
questions.explanation: The review has changed the speaker’s attention: instead of simply reading, they are looking for evidence that the reviewer was right.

speak: Start reflective and unhurried. Keep the repeated ‘sometimes ... sometimes ...’ rhythm light and natural. Slow slightly at ‘shouldn’t make much difference’, then make the contrast clear in ‘no longer reading the book / so much as checking’. Read the final sentence calmly, as a small realisation rather than a grand lesson.
review: Flow: saving the book for the perfect moment → delaying for weeks → finally starting → review contaminates attention → recognising the new reading goal → removing the phone → dry realisation that preparation itself had become the obstacle. Useful chunks: ‘make much difference’, ‘not so much A as B’, and ‘In the end, ...’.
